Three money questions. Only thirty percent pass.
One. A hundred dollars at two percent a year, for five years. More than a hundred and two, exactly, or less?
Two. You earn one percent. Prices rise two percent. Can you buy more, the same, or less?
Three. True or false: one company's stock is safer than a stock fund.
In a big US survey, only about thirty percent got all three.
But seventy percent rated their own money knowledge four or higher, out of seven.
So did you pass? Tell me in the comments.
